--k-cc-column-base.note: The mockup's 760/560 are the BASE, at reading size M. The effective column is the base × `--k-prose-scale` (kotatsu-chrome.css §2/§3, `body[data-k-prose-scale]`), so a bigger reading size widens the column in step and the measure holds at ~75 characters per line — reader-polish v0 finding 1: on a 3440 monitor the 15px/760px column owned 22% of the track, and the honest fix is bigger type at the same measure, never a wider measure (75 CPL is already the top of the comfortable range). At scale 1 the calc is byte-identical to the old literals. `shell/rail-collapse.js` reads the BASE and the scale as two separate numbers (a calc() custom property does not parseFloat), so keep them plain: a px length and a unitless number. `--k-cc-track-extra` (registered above; written by css/mes-variants.css for looks that trade avatar width for art) is the one additive term — it widens the track so the MEASURE survives the look, it never widens the measure.

--k-cc-composer-fill.note: The composer's own fill, and the one token §4 had to mint rather than borrow. `--k-inset-fill` is the INTERIOR card stop — 55% of `--k-surface-sunken` (kotatsu-chrome.css:195), minted for inline drawers and roster rows that sit ON an already-opaque panel, where the other 45% reveals that panel and nothing else. The rails composer has no such parent: `#k-center` paints no background (shell-frame.css §1), so under the pill that 45% was reading straight through to `#bg1`, and core's `backdrop-filter` was the only thing standing between a photographic background and the line being typed. With the blur gone (§4, composer performance v0 §8 C1) the fill has to hold contrast by itself, so it takes the alpha `--k-chrome-fill`'s bottom stop already uses for chrome that rides over the app background (kotatsu-chrome.css:187-189). Same colour, same border, same vocabulary, and the pack values are why that is not a cheat: the alpha only matters in proportion to how far the backdrop is from `--k-surface-sunken`, and under the composer it is barely anywhere. The move costs `0.37 × (sunken − backdrop)` per channel — at most ~6/255 against the bare gradient bottom in Blue Hour, low single digits in both packs once the ambient glow that actually sits under the pill is in the mix (tokens.css `--k-app-backdrop`). That is the point: a field that stops depending on a blur, not a field that looks like a performance mode. Arithmetic, not a measurement — the eye check is the shell QA pass.

Every other bubble, and every user bubble (they never carry swipes), stays symmetric.

--k-rc-chevron.default: linear-gradient(45deg, transparent var(--k-rc-chevron-a), var(--k-rc-chevron-ink) var(--k-rc-chevron-a), var(--k-rc-chevron-ink) var(--k-rc-chevron-b), transparent var(--k-rc-chevron-b)), linear-gradient(135deg, transparent var(--k-rc-chevron-a), var(--k-rc-chevron-ink) var(--k-rc-chevron-a), var(--k-rc-chevron-ink) var(--k-rc-chevron-b), transparent var(--k-rc-chevron-b))
--k-rc-chevron.note: The chevron. Replaces `/img/down-arrow.svg`'s frozen `#888888` triangle — see the header for why this is gradients and not a data: URI, and the parameters block for why the recipe is declared HERE, on the control, and not up there with its own parameters. Declared once; §2f reuses it.

--k-rc-chevron-ink.note: Chevron Two diagonal bands, each clipped to its own `--k-rc-chevron-arm` square: 45deg puts a "\" through the left square, 135deg a "/" through the right one, and the two squares are laid edge to edge so the strokes meet at the bottom — a 10x5 stroked chevron with the arm angle a designer would draw. The `a`/`b` stops are the band edges: the gradient line across a 5px square at 45° is 5√2 ≈ 7.07px long, so `50% ± weight/2` in px IS the stroke width measured perpendicular to the stroke. The ink is a var, not a literal, on purpose — it is what makes this repaintable. A pack retints every chevron in the app by declaring `--k-rc-chevron-ink`, and the hover rules retint one control the same way. The RECIPE itself (`--k-rc-chevron`) is deliberately NOT declared here, next to its own parameters, and that is not an oversight. A custom property's computed value is its token stream WITH ITS var()s ALREADY SUBSTITUTED, resolved on the element that declares it — so a `--k-rc-chevron` declared on `body` would bake in body's ink and then be inherited already-frozen. Overriding `--k-rc-chevron-ink` on `select:hover` would compile, apply, and change absolutely nothing. It lives on the `select` rule instead, §2a, where the substitution happens on the control itself and the hover override is in scope.

The stock treatment was a flat opaque `--crimson70a` slab that went FULL `--fullred` on hover — a solid red brick in a sheet full of hairlines.

--k-rc-hairline.note: Same recipe as `--k-lib-hairline` / `--k-studio-hairline`, restated rather than borrowed: those are sheet-local to their own slices. --k-rcf-hairline-lit.note: Hover: the same hairline, leaned on. Not a colour change, a pressure change.

--k-set-title-size.note: Fixed now, not a clamp: the header is one literal 49px row, not a shape that negotiates with viewport width.

--k-set-weave-gap.note: The weave's column gutter, and the color grid's. Wider than the row gap so the two columns read as columns rather than as one wrapped list.

--k-studio-field-fill.note: Fields read as CUT INTO the panel — Kirara's move. The darkest surface token there is.
